Privacy

This notice is a plain-language summary for Veylet Studio (Australia). Last updated 19 November 2026. It is not legal advice.

Changes in this version.

This version of the notice takes effect on [effective date — owner sets at release]. It adds what the app records about captures, practice-room results, what shared walkthrough pages count for the agent, crash reports, notifications, room names, listing details, how long we keep these records and how to delete them. The app does not send the new capture records, and shared walkthrough pages do not send viewer insights, before this version takes effect.

What we collect.

Your email address, which is how you sign in and how we reach you. The captures you send us, and the walkthroughs made from them. Your plan’s purchase state from the App Store — whether a subscription is active, which product it is, and when it renews — never your card number, your Apple ID or your payment details, which Apple keeps and we never see. And counts of use: walkthroughs sent, accepted, handoffs created and revoked, so the plan’s allowance can be counted and your desk can show it. We ask for no more than the work needs.

What we never do.

We never sell, rent or trade personal information. Your captures are not used to advertise to you and are not passed to anyone outside Veylet without your instruction.

Page counts.

veylet.com counts page views with Vercel Web Analytics, which uses no cookies and stores no personal identifiers: it counts the page address (without query strings or fragments), the referrer, the country and the device type in aggregate. Vercel may process this outside Australia. Google Analytics still runs only after you allow it.

Optional website analytics.

Google Analytics 4 loads only after you allow Analytics in Privacy choices. It helps us understand visits to our home, getting-started, offer and privacy pages, including page views and basic device and session information. You can reject it and still use the website and every form. We save your choice in this browser for up to 180 days. Advertising tracking, including Meta Pixel, is off. Email tips consent is separate: joining the waitlist or choosing email tips does not enable website measurement.

What analytics receives.

Our site's page-view events use a fixed public page title and its canonical address, without query strings or fragments, and an empty referrer field. We do not include names, email addresses, form answers, property details, account IDs or private links in our event fields. We may include approved campaign labels from public links. We do not run this measurement on enquiry or application forms, account, sign-in, app, private walkthrough or customer sharing pages. Our site does not send custom click, form, waitlist or purchase events.

Google's processing.

After you allow Analytics, Google can receive technical information such as your IP address and browser details and use analytics cookies or device identifiers. Google may process information outside Australia. Its Privacy Policy explains its processing, retention and deletion practices. We do not enable advertising personalisation through this analytics setup.

Changing your choice.

Open Privacy choices on any of these four pages to change or withdraw consent. Withdrawal stops future optional measurement and clears the optional identifiers this website can control. If analytics is running, the page reloads to stop it. Withdrawal cannot recall information already sent to Google. Contact us about access or deletion requests.

Enquiries.

Walkthrough enquiries from /request are stored in our database with Supabase in Sydney (ap-southeast-2), and Resend emails us a copy and emails you a confirmation. Waitlist sign-ups are stored in our database with Supabase in Sydney (ap-southeast-2). Resend, an email service that may process information outside Australia, emails us a copy of your answers and emails you a confirmation. The request form is for assessing a walkthrough. Do not send access codes, identity documents or private client images. When you arrive from a campaign link, this browser keeps that link’s campaign labels (such as utm_source=instagram), whether it came from a Meta or Google ad, and the Veylet page you arrived on, for the visit; a waitlist sign-up includes them so we know which link brought you. The click identifiers Meta and Google add to links are not kept.

Accounts.

New accounts are admitted in weekly groups from the waitlist; for help, contact Veylet support at support@veylet.com. Once an account is admitted, signing in with an email address either returns you to an account that already exists for that address or creates one — there is no separate sign-up step, and the first sign-in is the account being made. It is a hosted identity so the same person can use the website and the iPhone app. Identity and related records are stored with Supabase in Sydney (ap-southeast-2). Sign-in is not operator approval and is not payment. We never merge two accounts that share an email address.

Practice results.

After sign-in, the app automatically sends completed practice results to help evaluate and improve the guidance: pass or fail, duration, saved-view and direction counts, failure reasons, app build and device model. Up to 20 pending results wait on your device for a connection or service response. Results made while signed in remain associated with that account; a result made while signed out is sent under the next account to sign in. Practice images, camera positions and depth are not included.

Local journey events.

The app keeps up to 200 events about capture and account journeys on your device, excluded from backups. They contain fixed action words, capture and tour IDs and, when signed in, your account ID, plus app build, environment, counts and timings, not typed names, addresses, images or GPS location. These events are not uploaded: journey uploads remain off, and events recorded while uploads are off are never sent later.

Diagnostics and support.

Crash, hang, CPU, disk-write and launch summaries stay on your device, capped at 20 reports and 64 KB, excluded from backups. A redacted report is shared only when you choose the diagnostic support action and send it through the share menu. The report omits account IDs, email, captures, space names, file paths and location, but a file you send may remain attached to identifying support correspondence. Other messages and files you choose to send support are used to answer your request and kept only as long as needed for that work.

Activity and walkthrough Insights.

Account Activity records capture outcomes and your own read status so the app and website can show the same updates. Reading an update does not resolve its task. Walkthrough Insights reports recorded opens and contact or sharing taps; these are not unique visitors, confirmed enquiries or completed deliveries. A separate stop-engagement collector is prepared but disabled. If enabled after review, it will use a temporary identifier for one visit, the walkthrough revision, numbered stops reached and active foreground time, without cookies, cross-visit identity, gaze or physical movement. Private previews, explicit owner-preview links and bundled samples do not submit these observations. An anonymous direct open of a public link cannot be distinguished from another visitor. Missing observations are not reported as zero.

Your records.

Spaces you save hold a name, a category and a suburb or city. They must not hold a street address, unit number, access code, identity document or private client image, and the desk rejects an address-shaped location. You can download a file of your spaces and tours from your desk at any time, and ask us to correct anything that is wrong.

Room captures on your device.

Veylet Capture saves camera photographs, LiDAR depth and camera-position data locally so you can inspect and export a capture. When you choose Send, photos, LiDAR depth and camera positions are uploaded with the capture manifest for processing in your workspace. These environment scans describe the space, not your GPS location. A copy of your originals stays on your device. When you export through the device's share menu, the package goes to the app or recipient you choose. Device backups and third-party sharing services follow your settings with those services.

Listing details and photos.

The headline, description, bedroom, bathroom and car-space numbers and photos you add to a listing in the app are saved on this iPhone only; Veylet does not upload them. Photos come only from your own photo library, after you confirm you own or are licensed to use them. Veylet never copies photos or text from a listing website. When a walkthrough is embedded on a website, the embed tells us only that website’s address, never the page it is on, so views can be counted per website.

Tour files.

When you send a reconstructed tour from Veylet Capture, the package is stored privately for the property's workspace. Active workspace members can open finished tours for review. Unfinished uploads remain available only to their uploader while that membership is active. A client handoff lets anyone holding its link open the shared tour. Street addresses, access codes and ID documents do not belong in these records.

Room names.

You can rename a room while you review a walkthrough. The name is stored with that walkthrough and shown to anyone who opens its link. Name the room only (for example Main bedroom): never a person’s name, a street address or an access code. The capture records below use the room’s type, never the name you give it.

How walkthroughs are processed.

Walkthroughs are processed automatically on cloud GPUs in the United States, run by Modal, so your capture is sent outside Australia for processing. No Veylet staff member views a capture as part of normal processing. An automatic quality check decides whether a walkthrough is ready for your review. An AI visual check is planned; it will be listed here before it is switched on.

What the app records about captures.

To see where capturing gets hard, and to check the rooms the app shows you against the rooms we count, Veylet Capture records a short note at each step below. These records are linked to your Veylet account, never include addresses, names, text you type, photos or your location, and are deleted after 13 months or when you delete your account.

  • When you start a capture, the app records that a capture started, with a random capture number and whether it is room by room.
  • When a room starts, the app records its type from our list (for example Bedroom or Hall, never a name you type) and its number in the capture.
  • When a room ends, the app records its type, how many photos and standing spots it saved and how many seconds it took.
  • When you finish a capture, the app records how many rooms and photos it has, the number of rooms it expects to use and how long it took.
  • When a capture ends without being finished, the app records the step it ended at, the app’s reason code, the type of room you were in and the counts so far.
  • When you send a capture, the app records the number of rooms it showed you, so we can compare it with the rooms we count.
  • When you approve a walkthrough, the app records that it was approved, with the walkthrough’s random identifier.
  • When you use the share kit, the app records which option you used (link, embed code, QR code or video), with the walkthrough’s random identifier.

Each note holds only counts, seconds, yes or no, and words from a fixed list. Notes wait on this iPhone, outside device backups, until they are sent, and are stored with Supabase in Sydney (ap-southeast-2).

Practice-room results.

When you finish a practice room, the app sends the result to your account: whether it passed, the reasons it did not, how long it took, how many views it saved, how many directions it covered, the app build and the iPhone model. It never sends the practice photos, depth or camera positions. Up to 20 results wait on this iPhone until someone is signed in; a result made while nobody was signed in is sent with the next account that signs in.

Client handoff links.

A handoff is an unlisted link you choose to create for one tour. Anyone holding that link can open the walkthrough; it asks the client for no account, and Revoke stops it working. Handoff and preview pages are excluded from search engines. Do not pass a link to anyone who should not see the space.

Shared walkthrough usage.

Shared walkthrough pages record anonymous usage for the agent who shared them: that the link was opened, how long the page stayed open, which rooms and stops were viewed and for how long, the direction looked from each stop, taps on Call, Email or Share, and the hostname of a website that embeds the walkthrough. This uses no cookies and nothing stored in the browser, and it does not record a name, an account, an IP address or anything else that identifies the viewer.

Viewer insights.

When someone views a walkthrough, the page records how many stops they reached, the stop they left on and the seconds spent in each type of room, with no cookie and nothing that identifies the viewer. Room types come from the app’s fixed list (for example Bedroom or Hall), never a room’s own name. The summary is added to the one time-on-page record a visit already sends, for the agent who shared the walkthrough. Adding ?analytics=off to a walkthrough link stops this summary for that browser tab; the usage described under Shared walkthrough usage is still counted.

Crash reports.

If you have chosen to share analytics with app developers in your iPhone’s settings (Privacy & Security › Analytics & Improvements), Apple sends us crash reports for Veylet Capture. Apple decides what they hold, and we do not link them to your Veylet account. The app also keeps short crash and performance summaries on this iPhone; they leave it only when you choose Send diagnostics to Veylet support under Account › About.

A later app version may add a switch to send crash reports to us automatically. It will be off until you turn it on. If you turn on crash reports, Veylet Capture sends a short report when the app crashes, hangs or uses too much power: the app and iOS version, the device model and where in the app’s code it happened. It contains no photos, captures, addresses, space names or account details, is not linked to your account, and is deleted after 90 days. You can turn it off in Account › About.

Notifications.

After your first send, if you allow notifications, the app gives us the push token Apple assigns to Veylet Capture on this iPhone. It is linked to your account and used only to tell you when a walkthrough is ready for review. The notification goes through Apple’s push notification service, which may process it outside Australia, and never shows a listing’s title or address. We stop using a token once Apple tells us it no longer works, and it is deleted with your account. To stop notifications, turn them off for Veylet Capture in your iPhone’s Settings.

Deleting your account.

Ask in the app or on your desk at veylet.com/account. We complete the deletion within 30 days and confirm when it is done. You cannot undo it yourself. When it completes, your account, its spaces and its walkthroughs are removed, every handoff link and embed stops working, and hosting of every released walkthrough ends with them — deletion ends hosting at once, without the 14 days that follow the end of a plan. Remove the links and embeds from your listing too, because copies people already downloaded cannot be recalled.

What deletion covers.

Hosted capture files, generated walkthroughs and the account records used to deliver them are removed. Once removal starts, these files cannot be restored through your account. Copies on your own device, exported files and copies already downloaded by someone else are outside this account deletion. Contact us about any copies held separately by the studio.

How long we keep these records.

Capture records and practice-room results: 13 months, or until you delete your account if that is sooner. Viewer usage and viewer insights on shared walkthroughs: 13 months, or until the walkthrough is deleted if that is sooner. Crash reports sent to us automatically: 90 days. Push tokens: until Apple tells us a token no longer works, or until you delete your account. Records still waiting on your iPhone are removed when you delete the app.

Deleting these records.

Delete my account, under Account in the app, or the deletion request on your desk removes the capture records, practice-room results, push tokens and room names described here with the rest of your account, as set out under Deleting your account. To see or correct these records, or to ask about this notice, write to support@veylet.com.

Limited records we retain.

Invoices, receipts and minimal records of payments, accepted services and deletion may be retained for accounting and legal obligations. These retained records do not provide access to your imagery, captures or walkthroughs. Deleting a Veylet account does not cancel a subscription billed by Apple; manage that subscription in your Apple account.

Cloudflare provides hosting and website performance measurements. Hosting logs may also exist at Vercel and Supabase. An App Store subscription is sold and charged by Apple; this public site does not collect card numbers.

Ask to access, correct or delete your account data: support@veylet.com. We keep enquiry mail as needed to assess a job, then no longer than the work requires. If you are not satisfied with how we handled a privacy question, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

Veylet Studio is operated by Yo-Da Lai, a sole trader (ABN 84 992 526 369) in south-east Queensland, Australia, who is responsible for the personal information described here.
